title: Sodium-ion batteries establish a foothold as a lithium alternative
gist: Wood Mackenzie says sodium-ion batteries are entering commercial production with over 70 GWh of supply agreements, reaching cell-level cost parity with LFP among leaders by end-2026 but module and system parity only after 2030. Despite a higher upfront cost ($229/kWh vs $200/kWh for LFP), sodium-ion offers 21% lower total cost of ownership, and policy (China tax exemptions, US tariffs and 45X credits, EU Battery Regulation, India incentives) is a bigger driver than cost; LFP remains the bankable choice for projects today.

insights.claim: Sodium-ion batteries are entering commercial production backed by over 70 GWh of supply agreements, which Wood Mackenzie reads as downstream confidence in the chemistry.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sodium-ion is moving from lab to contracted volumes, a real diversification option from lithium.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects sodium-ion cell-level cost parity with lithium iron phosphate among market leaders by end-2026, but module- and system-level parity only after 2030.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Near-term sodium-ion threat to LFP system economics is limited.

insights.claim: Ankita Chauhan of Wood Mackenzie says sodium-ion wins on supply chain security, cycle life and wide thermal tolerance, with geopolitical supply advantages and cross-temperature performance driving near-term commercialisation.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sodium-ion's near-term niche is cold-climate and supply-security-sensitive deployments.
insights.quote: SIB wins on supply chain security, cycle life and wide thermal threshold
insights.locator: SIB wins on supply chain security

insights.claim: BYD has 30 GWh of planned sodium-ion manufacturing capacity in China and CATL targets at least 1 GWh of sodium-ion shipments by end-2026, with China's 2026-35 learning rate of 18-20% the most mature in the sector.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Chinese incumbents are set to dominate sodium-ion as they did LFP.

insights.claim: Sodium-ion storage costs more upfront, about $229/kWh globally versus $200/kWh for LFP, but delivers 21% lower total cost of ownership over a 20-year project life by eliminating augmentation events and lowering opex.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: TCO advantage could favor sodium-ion for long-life storage once bankability is proven.
insights.locator: Higher upfront cost, lower lifetime cost

insights.claim: China's export controls, India's underdeveloped supply chain, slow US gigafactory expansion and German trade policies risk constraining near-term sodium-ion growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Trade frictions cap sodium-ion deployment outside China near term.
insights.locator: Higher upfront cost, lower lifetime cost

insights.claim: China's July 2026 reimposition of a lithium-ion consumption tax exempts sodium-ion through end-2028, while LFP faces a 2% levy from September 2026 rising to 4% from September 2027.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Tax differential directly tilts Chinese demand toward sodium-ion.
insights.locator: Policy outpaces cost as the key

insights.claim: In the US, Section 301 tariffs of about 58% on Chinese energy storage cells plus IRA 45X manufacturing credits structurally incentivise domestic sodium-ion production, while the EU Battery Regulation's carbon-footprint disclosure and India's $1.25 billion incentive scheme also support the chemistry.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Policy creates a protected market for non-Chinese sodium-ion manufacturers.
insights.locator: Policy outpaces cost as the key

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie analyst Priya Shrivastava says 2030-2035 is when sodium-ion economics decisively shift, while LFP remains the bankable choice for 2-4 hour storage projects deployed today.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: LFP suppliers keep the storage market this decade; sodium-ion is a post-2030 story.
insights.quote: The 2030-2035 window is where the economics decisively shift

insights.claim: Sodium-ion still must scale production, refine cell materials and build a performance track record, so the most probable outcome is a multi-chemistry battery market with technologies optimized for different applications and durations.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sodium-ion complements rather than displaces lithium; lithium demand risk is moderate.
